name: Morb
Effect: Emits 200 g of Polluted Oxygen periodically (average 20 g/s)
description:
Morb
Pest Critter


The Morb is a versatile scavenger, capable of breaking down and consuming dead matter from most plant and animal species.
It poses a severe disease risk to humans due to the thick slime it excretes to surround its inner cartilage structures.A single teaspoon of Morb slime can contain up to a quadrillion bacteria that work to deter would-be predators and liquefy its food.
Petting a Morb is not recommended.

name: Dartle
Effect: Seeks nearby mature Dew Dripper Plants to harvest
description:
Dartle
Domesticable Critter


Dartles are docile reptilian critters whose existence centers around maximum energy conservation.This species was once known as the fastest land-based critter in existence. However, its deep aversion to physical exertion has grown stronger than its desire to escape predation. Researchers are uncertain what, if anything, the Dartle is saving its energy for.

Initial Egg Chances: Hatch Egg: 96.08 %Stone Hatch Egg: 1.96 %Sage Hatch Egg: 1.96 %
description:
Hatches

name: Floxes
Shearing: 1 cycle of food grows 16.67 % Antler Growth over 1 cycleShears for 360 kg Wood
description:
Flox
Domesticable Critter


Evenly distributed throughout the Flox's dense overcoat are countless vibrissae-like hairs that transmit detailed sensory information about its environment, allowing it to detect changes as subtle as the shift in another creature's mood.Floxes avoid overstimulation by whipping their tails to release the pent-up energy. Because these tactile hairs are so sensitive, they cannot be safely shorn.Flox antlers, however, are nerveless and cumbersome. Handlers who unburden them of this cranial load are often rewarded with the critter's long, slow blinks of contentment.

name: Bammoths
Shearing: 1 cycle of food grows 10 % Fur Growth over 1 cycleShears for 5 kg Reed Fiber
Tags: Creature, BagableCreature, Walker, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature, LargeCreature
description:
Bammoth
Domesticable Critter


The Bammoth is one of the oldest species on record, with ancient skeletal remains dating back approximately 10,000 years.This placid herbivore is known for its unique body language: an angry young Bammoth expresses displeasure by flopping down dramatically in front of its opponent, while older creatures with limited mobility will sit facing away from the source of their annoyance.Licking the ground in front of a caregiver can be a sign of either deep affection or mineral deficiency.

name: Jawbo
Tags: SwimmingCreature, Swimmer, Creature, CreatureBrain, BagableCreature, LargeCreature, OriginalCreature
description:
Jawbo
Aquatic Critter


While the Jawbo may be terrifying to behold, in truth it is quite harmless for trained handlers.A disproportionately sized mandible makes it impossible for this critter to properly chew its food, necessitating a preference for prey that are small enough to be swallowed whole.Though much of its DNA suggests that the Jawbo evolved in isolation, it does share a small number of genetic markers with serrasalmids such as the Pacu. Familial connection, however, does not preclude consideration as a food source.

name: Dreckos
Shearing: Scale Growth 12.5 %/cycleRequires Hydrogen Gas atmosphereShears for 2 kg Reed Fiber
description:
Dreckos
Critter Species


Dreckos are a reptilian species boasting billions of microscopic hairs on their feet, allowing them to stick to and climb most surfaces.
The tail of the Drecko, called the "train", is purely for decoration and can be lost or shorn without harm to the animal.As a result, Drecko fibers are often farmed for use in textile production.Caring for Dreckos is a fulfilling endeavor thanks to their companionable personalities.Some domestic Dreckos have even been known to respond to their own names.

name: Lumbs
Effect: Seeks nearby mature plants to harvest
Tags: Creature, Walker, BagableCreature, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature, LargeCreature
description:
Lumb
Domesticable Critter


While other creatures with the Lumb's low forebrain neuron count rapidly become extinct, these docile creatures are uniquely positioned for survival.Their large size and spiny protrusions make them unappealing to most predators. Anecdotal evidence also suggests that smaller species will sometimes adopt orphaned Lumbs.Some experts theorize that this may be motivated by a desire to benefit from the Lumb's genetic muscular condition (akin to restless leg syndrome), which causes them to regularly pound the earth in such a way as to cause nearby plants to drop desirable foods.

name: Moos
Milking: 0.9 cycles of food replenishes 25 % Brackene Supply over 1 cycleMilks for 200 kg Brackene
description:
Moos
Critter Species


Little is currently known of the Moo due to its alien nature and origin.It is capable of surviving in zero gravity conditions and no atmosphere, and its method of reproduction has yet to be discovered.
The Moo has an even temperament and cohabits well with others in a farm setting.

name: Rover
description:
Rover
Scouting Robot


The Rover is a planetary scout robot programmed to land on and mine Planetoids where sending a Duplicant would put them unneccessarily in danger.Rovers are programmed to be very pleasant and social when interacting with other beings. However, an unintended consequence of this programming is that the socialized robots tended to experience the same work slow-downs due to loneliness and low morale.To compensate for this, the Rover was programmed to have two distinct personalities it can switch between to have pleasant in-depth conversations with itself during long stints alone.

name: Rhex
Shearing: 1 cycle of food grows 25 % Feather Growth over 1 cycleShears for 4 kg Feather Fiber
Tags: Creature, Walker, BagableCreature, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature, LargeCreature
description:
Rhex
Carnivorous Critter


For all their bluster, Rhexes are emotionally sensitive creatures that thrive on positive reinforcement, especially words of affirmation.These sightless apex predators have exceptionally acidic gastric juices that kill most known bacteria and toxins, enabling them to safely digest their prey. This protective mechanism renders them susceptible to chronic ulcers if food is not readily available.The Rhex's tailfeather can be shorn to harvest fibers for textile production. Rhexes don't mind this - some even enjoy it.

name: Pacus
Initial Egg Chances: Pacu Egg: 96.08 %Tropical Pacu Egg: 1.96 %Gulp Fish Egg: 1.96 %
Tags: SwimmingCreature, Swimmer, BagableCreature, Creature, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature
description:
Pacus
Critter Species


The Pacu fish is often interpreted as possessing a vacant stare due to its large and unblinking eyes, yet they are remarkably bright and friendly creatures.
Despite descending from the Pacu, the Gulp Fish is unique enough both in genetics and behavior to be considered its own subspecies.
It is said that the average Pacu intelligence is comparable to that of a dog, and that they are capable of learning and distinguishing from over twenty human faces.

name: Mimika
Effect: Seeks nearby plants and applies Pollinated (Mimika)
Tags: Creature, Flyer, BagableCreature, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature, Pollinator
description:
Mimika
Critter?


Mimikas are difficult to categorize. Biologists theorize that the Mimika Bud engages in this rare variation of reproductive mimicry to improve seed-dispersal and survive the extinction of key species native to its original habitat.These charming moth-like organisms feature a microscopic cluster of phytoprotein "brain" cells and are driven by a singular instinct to tend to their host plants.Due to a monogenic malfunction, however, this plant-tending behavior benefits all of the flora in its area except its own.

name: Gnit
Effect: applies Gnit Stung to others, granting self Stung A Target (1 Cycle)   on Critters (0.5 cycles)   -1 Happiness   on Duplicants (1 cycle)  +10% Stress/cycle   +5 Sneeziness   -1 Athletics
description:
Gnit
Pest Critter


The Gnit is an insectoid critter that relies on supplementary nutrients and minerals from Duplicants and other critters to mitigate the outsized energy requirements of its reproductive system.Gnits' antennae double as maxillary palps equipped with finely tuned olfactory receptor neurons that enable them to pinpoint nutrient sources from a great distance.These same receptors activate the insectoid's flight response upon detecting certain changes in an organism's respiration, such as the sharp intake of breath that precedes a fatal counter-attack.

name: Shine Bugs
Effect: 1,800 Lux (Well Lit) (Range: 5 tiles)60 rads/cycle (Mostly Safe) (Range: 6 Tiles)
Tags: Creature, Flyer, BagableCreature, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature, LightSource
description:
Shine Bugs
Critter Species


The bioluminescence of the Shine Bug's body serves the social purpose of finding and communicating with others of its kind.
It is not uncommon for Shine Bugs to mistakenly approach inanimate sources of light in search of a friend.
It is unwise to touch a Shine Bug's wing blades directly due to the extremely fragile nature of their membranes.
The Shine Bug can be pet anywhere else along its body, although it is advised that care still be taken due to the generally delicate nature of its exoskeleton.

name: Pufts
Initial Egg Chances: Puft Egg: 94.23 %Puft Prince Egg: 1.92 %Dense Puft Egg: 1.92 %Squeaky Puft Egg: 1.92 %
description:
Pufts
Critter Species


The Puft is a mellow creature whose limited brainpower is largely dedicated to sustaining its basic life processes.
Pufts often have a collection of asymmetric teeth lining the ridge of their mouths, although this feature is entirely vestigial as Pufts do not consume solid food.Instead, a baleen-like mesh of keratin at the back of the Puft's throat works to filter out tiny organisms and food particles from the air.Unusable air is expelled back out the Puft's posterior trunk, along with waste material and any indigestible particles or pathogens which it then evacuates as solid biomass.
The Puft is an easy creature to raise for first time handlers given its wholly amiable disposition and suggestible nature.It is unusually tolerant of human handling and will allow itself to be patted or scratched nearly anywhere on its fuzzy body, including, unnervingly, directly on any of its three eyeballs.
A specialized air bladder in the Puft's chest cavity stores varying concentrations of gas, allowing it to control its buoyancy and float effortlessly through the air.Combined with extremely lightweight and elastic skin, the Puft is capable of maintaining flotation indefinitely with negligible energy expenditure. Its orientation and balance, meanwhile, are maintained by counterweighted formations of bone located in its otherwise useless legs.

name: Spigot Seal
Effect: Bonbon Tree Seed (20% Chance on emission)
description:
Spigot Seal
Domesticable Critter


Spigot Seals are named for the hollow, cone-shaped glabellar protrusion that allows them to siphon nourishment directly from plants into the digestive sac located at the cone's base.In order to draw nutritious fluids through this "straw," the Spigot Seal compresses its nasal cavity and pumps its tongue up into its soft palate repeatedly, creating a vacuum.Mealtimes are concluded by lapping at the air to reopen the airways and prevent accidental asphyxiation.Many handlers enjoy teaching this critter to clap its flippers, only to discover that there is no reliable method of limiting how often or how loudly the behavior is repeated.

name: Pips
description:
Pip
Domesticable Critter


Pips are a member of the Rodentia order with a strong caching instinct that causes them to find and bury small objects, most often seeds.
It is unknown whether their caching behavior is a compulsion or a form of entertainment, as the Pip relies primarily on bark and wood for its survival.
Although the Pip lacks truly opposable thumbs, it nonetheless has highly dexterous paws that allow it to rummage through most tight to reach spaces in search of seeds and other treasures.

name: Divergents
Effect: Seeks nearby plants and applies Pollinated (Sweetle)
Tags: Creature, BagableCreature, Walker, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature, Pollinator
description:
Divergent
Domesticable Critter


'Divergent' is the name given to the two different genders of one species, the Sweetle and the Grubgrub, both of which are able to reproduce asexually and tend to Grubfruit Plants.When tending to the Grubfruit Plant, both gender variants of the Divergent display the exact same behaviors, however the Grubgrub possesses slightly more tiny facial hair which helps in pollinating the plants and stimulates faster growth.

name: Slicksters
Initial Egg Chances: Slickster Egg: 96.08 %Molten Slickster Egg: 1.96 %Longhair Slickster Egg: 1.96 %
description:
Slicksters
Critter Species


Slicksters are a unique creature most renowned for their ability to exude hydrocarbon waste that is nearly identical in makeup to crude oil.The two tufts atop a Slickster's head are called rhinophores, and help guide the Slickster toward breathable carbon dioxide.
Positioned on either side of the Major Rhinophores are Minor Rhinophores, which specialize in mechanical reception and detect air pressure around the Slickster. These send signals to the brain to contract or expand its air sacks accordingly.
Slicksters are amicable creatures famous amongst breeders for their good personalities and smiley faces.Slicksters rarely if ever nip at human handlers, and are considered non-ideal house pets only for the oily mess they involuntarily leave behind wherever they go.

name: Pokeshells
Tags: Creature, BagableCreature, Walker, CrabFriend, CreatureBrain, Amphibious, OriginalCreature
description:
Pokeshell
Domesticable Critter


Pokeshells are bottom-feeding invertebrates that consume the waste and discarded food left behind by other creatures.
They have formidably sized claws that fold safely into their shells for protection when not in use.
As Pokeshells mature they must periodically shed portions of their exoskeletons to make room for new growth.
Although the most dramatic sheds occur early in a Pokeshell's adolescence, they will continue growing and shedding throughout their adult lives, until the day they eventually die.

name: Plug Slugs
Effect: Produces Power at Night: See Here for details
Initial Egg Chances: Plug Slug Egg: 96.08 %Smog Slug Egg: 1.96 %Sponge Slug Egg: 1.96 %
Tags: Walker, Amphibious, Creature, BagableCreature, CreatureBrain, OriginalCreature
description:
Plug Slug
Domesticable Critter


Plug Slugs are fuzzy gastropoda that are able to cling to walls and ceilings thanks to an extreme triboelectric effect caused by friction between their fur and various surfaces.This same phenomomen allows the Plug Slug to generate a significant amount of static electricity that can be converted into power.The increased amount of static electricity a Plug Slug can generate when domesticated is due to the internal vibration, or contented 'humming', they demonstrate when all their needs are met.

name: Shove Voles
Tags: Creature, BagableCreature, Walker, CreatureBrain, Digger, OriginalCreature
description:
Shove Vole
Domesticable Critter


The Shove Vole is a unique creature that possesses two fully developed sets of lungs, allowing it to hold its breath during the long periods it spends underground.
Drill-shaped keratin structures circling the Vole's body aids its ability to drill at high speeds through most natural materials.

name: Critter
description:
"This critter is trapped within a door, tile, or confined space"
"Sounds uncomfortable!"

name: Beeta
description:
Beeta
Aggressive Critter


Beetas are insectoid creatures that enjoy a symbiotic relationship with the radioactive environment they thrive in.Much like the honey bee gathers nectar and processes it to honey, the Beeta turns Uranium Ore into Enriched Uranium through a complex process of isotope separation inside the Beeta Hive.When first observing the Beeta's enrichment process, many scientists note with surprise just how much more efficient the cooperative combination of insect and hive is when compared to even the most advanced industrial processes.
